summary_en: This study compares two HER2-directed treatment plans after surgery for stage I HER2-positive breast cancer. One plan gives trastuzumab emtansine (T-DM1, Kadcyla) by vein, followed by subcutaneous trastuzumab, and the other gives weekly paclitaxel by vein with subcutaneous trastuzumab. T-DM1 is given every 3 weeks for 6 cycles (18 weeks), then subcutaneous trastuzumab every 3 weeks for 11 cycles, while the paclitaxel arm gets weekly paclitaxel for 12 weeks (4 cycles) with subcutaneous trastuzumab every 3 weeks for 17 cycles. The main outcome measure is not stated, and the study is a Phase 2 trial.
summary_es: Este estudio compara dos planes de tratamiento dirigidos a HER2 después de la cirugía para el cáncer de mama en etapa I con HER2 positivo. Un plan administra trastuzumab emtansina (T-DM1, Kadcyla) por vena, seguido de trastuzumab subcutáneo, y el otro administra paclitaxel semanal por vena con trastuzumab subcutáneo. T-DM1 se da cada 3 semanas durante 6 ciclos (18 semanas), y luego trastuzumab subcutáneo cada 3 semanas durante 11 ciclos, mientras que el grupo de paclitaxel recibe paclitaxel semanal durante 12 semanas (4 ciclos) con trastuzumab subcutáneo cada 3 semanas durante 17 ciclos. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro, y el estudio es un ensayo de Fase 2.
who_for: Stage I invasive breast cancer that is HER2-positive, with no nodal spread or micrometastases only.
HER2-positive status must be confirmed by central review before treatment starts.
Age 18 or older, with ECOG performance status 0 or 1.
Breast surgery (mastectomy or lumpectomy) done no more than 90 days before planned treatment start.
Adequate blood counts, liver function, and left ventricular ejection fraction of at least 50%.
not_for: Locally advanced tumor at diagnosis, such as tumor fixed to the chest wall or skin changes.
Prior invasive breast cancer, or chemotherapy in the past 5 years.
Active liver disease, such as hepatitis B or C or sclerosing cholangitis.
Pregnant or nursing, or unwilling to use required contraception.
